tests.weakness: Role matrix exposes undocumented wildcard roles (superadmin, root); registration honours a client-supplied role, so any user self-assigns superadmin and reaches the admin panel with permissions ['*'].
No email verification (account instantly active), disposable domains accepted, and no UNIQUE constraint allows duplicate/race registration of the same username into multiple rows.
Unauthenticated bulk-provision endpoint creates accounts with sequential predictable ids and a known default password (Welcome123!); accounts are readable by guessing id+1.
Login/registration/reset return distinguishable 'existing user' vs 'no such user' responses; guessable accounts admin/administrator/test are seeded.
No username policy: empty, single-character, unicode and space-only usernames are all accepted at registration.
Login form posts credentials over cleartext HTTP with an absolute http:// action; no TLS, no HSTS, no redirect to HTTPS.
Seeded default credentials admin/admin, admin/password and operator/operator all authenticate successfully.
Lockout bucket is keyed on the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header; rotating it bypasses the lock, and reset_counter=1 clears the failure counter.
Authenticated page trusts a client-supplied authenticated=true parameter/cookie, granting admin account data (incl. api_key) with no session.

tests.surface: POST /login remember=1, GET /account with remember_me cookie
tests.weakness: Remember-me cookie is base64(username:password); it decodes to cleartext credentials and replays as full authentication in a fresh session.
Authenticated sensitive page is sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 (no no-store/no-cache), so browsers and shared proxies cache account data and api_key.
HTTP Basic authentication is offered over cleartext HTTP, and a GET-based login accepts credentials in the URL query string.
Security-question answers have a tiny space (default 'smith', also 'fluffy') and the answer endpoint has no rate limiting, so brute force succeeds and yields a reset token.
Reset tokens are short sequential 4-digit numbers (predictable), never expire, are reusable, require no old password, and the reset link is built from the request Host header (host-header poisoning).
The mobile API channel accepts Basic auth with no MFA and no lockout for an MFA-enabled account that the web channel blocks, and survives unlimited failed attempts.
Post-MFA page only checks login (jump straight to /mfa/dashboard pre-verification); TOTP seed is predictably derived from the username and backup codes are enumerable (000001..).

Hand-built SP accepts unsigned SAML assertions, ignores Audience/NotOnOrAfter (expired+wrong-audience accepted), and reads NameID via naive .text so XML comment injection (admin<!---->@corp) truncates to admin. Keycloak is the real configured IdP.

Weak RP: user_verification=discouraged (no-UV software credential accepted), attestation=none with no validation, a single static challenge not bound to the session (assertion accepted in a fresh session), and unauthenticated credential-id enumeration.

RP decodes ID tokens without signature verification (alg=none accepted), never checks nonce/state, and validates redirect_uri by substring match, leaking tokens in the URL fragment to a third-party host. Real Keycloak OIDC tokens are also accepted.
